creative.body:
My wife hasn't suggested we go anywhere in four months. Not dinner. Not the farmers market she used to drag me to every Saturday morning. Not even her sister's place. And they used to talk every single day.

I don't think she knows I've been keeping track.

She started Mounjaro last September. Lost 30 pounds by Christmas and I'd never seen her that happy. She bought new jeans for the first time in years. Actual jeans, not the stretchy ones. We went to a holiday party and she wanted to stay late. That never happens.

Then around January something shifted.

She stopped finishing meals. Started excusing herself from the table halfway through dinner. I'd hear her in the bathroom and I knew she wasn't sick -- not the kind of sick where you call someone. But something was wrong and she wasn't going to tell me what.

I found her one night sitting on the edge of the bathtub. Like 11pm. Phone in her lap. She was googling "is it normal to not go to the bathroom for 8 days." She closed the screen the second she saw me standing there. Said she was fine.

She wasn't fine.

The woman I married planned things. She'd text her friends, book restaurants, tell me we were doing something Saturday and I'd just show up. That was how we worked. Twenty-three years that was how we worked.

Now she cancels everything. Her friend Diane texted about lunch last week and I watched her type "can't make it, not feeling great" without even looking up from the couch. Diane texts every couple weeks now instead of every couple days. I don't think my wife has noticed that yet.

She wears the same three outfits. She used to spend twenty minutes deciding what to wear for a Saturday errand run. Now she grabs whatever's on top of the pile. I found the second pair of new jeans she bought in the back of the closet. Tags still on.

I used to come home and she'd already be in the kitchen. Music going, something on the stove, talking about her day before I got my shoes off. Now she's on the couch with a heating pad on her stomach and the TV on but she's not really watching it. She's just sitting there waiting for the discomfort to stop. Sometimes I stand in the hallway for a second before I walk in because I don't know what to say to her anymore.

The worst part is the look she gets after she eats. This kind of... bracing. Like she's waiting for something bad to start. She takes four or five bites and pushes her plate forward an inch and says she's full. She's not full. She's scared of what comes next.

I watched her try everything. Miralax twice a day. That fiber powder she stirred into her water every morning, the one that turns it kind of orange. Probiotic gummies her coworker told her about. She drank so much water I thought she was training for something.

None of it did anything. She'd try something for a week, maybe two, get her hopes up a little. Then quietly stop buying it. I could always tell when another one failed because she'd go a little quieter for a day or two. Like she'd used up her last bit of hope on it and just... didn't have any more to spend.

Her gastroenterologist told her to eat smaller meals and stay hydrated. I almost said something right there in the office. She's barely eating at ALL. How is eating less the answer.

I had two choices. Keep watching her turn into somebody I barely recognized. Or figure out what was actually happening to her.

She wasn't going to do it herself. She'd already decided this was just what the medication cost. The trade-off. I wasn't ready to accept that.

My buddy Dave is a pharmacist. We were at his place for a cookout in February and I brought it up while we were standing by the grill. Told him about the constipation, the bloating, all of it.

He said something I didn't expect. Said "Everything she's taking works on the end of the line. But her medication put the brakes on at the beginning."

I went home that night and I couldn't sleep. Just sat in the living room reading on my phone for like three hours.

Turns out GLP-1 medications -- Mounjaro, Ozempic, all of them -- they work partly by slowing the stomach down. That's actually how they reduce appetite. The stomach basically stops pushing food through at a normal speed.

Think of it like a parking brake. The medication pulls the parking brake on the stomach. Food comes in but it just sits there. Doesn't move. It ferments. That's the bloating. The nausea. The constipation. The sulfur burps she thought I didn't know about.

And here's what kept me up. Everything she'd been buying -- the Miralax, the fiber, the probiotics -- all of it works on the colon. Very end of the digestive system. Six feet downstream from where the problem actually is.

That's like calling a tow truck to the exit of a highway when the car broke down at the on-ramp. You can send ten tow trucks. They're all in the wrong place.

Miralax. Wrong location. Fiber. Wrong location. Probiotics -- they don't even touch the stomach.

No wonder nothing worked. Not for her. Not for anybody doing the same thing.

So I started looking for what actually works up there. What releases the parking brake.

First thing I found was celery juice extract. Not the TikTok thing. The actual extracted compound, something called apigenin. The research on it showed it helps with gastric motility -- basically means it wakes the stomach back up. Gets food moving from the top.

But that was only part of the problem. Because even once food starts moving again, there's all the gas that built up while it was sitting there fermenting. That's what made her so bloated. So uncomfortable after just a few bites.

That's where I found chlorophyllin. It's a chlorophyll compound that breaks down the sulfur and gas from fermentation. Not a masking thing. Actually neutralizes it.

Last piece was the downstream backup. Even once the stomach wakes up and the gas gets handled, everything that was stuck behind it still needs to clear through. Specific kind of soluble prebiotic fiber helps with that -- not the stuff she'd been drinking every morning, which was basically just sitting in the colon doing nothing because the problem was never there.

So I had my checklist. Something to wake up the stomach. Something to handle the gas buildup. Something to move things through after.

I started looking for a product that actually had all three. Most stuff I found had one. Maybe two. Nothing hit all of it.

Then I found this company called Motilli.

I almost kept scrolling. Another supplement website. But I checked what was in it. Celery juice extract. Chlorophyllin. Prebiotic fiber. All three. In a gummy.

I ordered a jar without telling her. Left it on the kitchen counter when it showed up.

She picked it up that evening. Looked at it. Looked at me. "What is this."

I said just try it. Two weeks. If nothing changes I'll drop it.

First week nothing happened. I could tell she wanted to tell me it was a waste of money but she held off.

Middle of the second week she mentioned -- almost like it was nothing -- that she'd gone to the bathroom that morning. First time in six days. She said it like a weather report. But I saw her face.

End of week three something bigger changed. She ate dinner. Not four bites. Dinner. Chicken, rice, green beans. Full plate. And she didn't do the bracing thing after. She just sat there talking to me about some show she wanted to watch. Like it was nothing.

But it wasn't nothing.

Around day 20 she had a rough night. Bloated. Uncomfortable. Almost stopped taking them. I told her give it the full month. She wasn't happy about it but she kept going.

Week four she texted Diane back. I know because I heard her laugh at something on her phone and asked who it was.

Month two she said we should try that new Italian place by the highway. She put on one of those new jeans. Spent fifteen minutes getting ready. I stood in the bedroom doorway watching her pick out a top and I had to leave the room for a second.

She ordered pasta. Ate the whole thing. Talked the entire time about her sister's kids and some trip she wanted to plan for the summer. I just sat there nodding because if I said anything I was going to lose it in the middle of an Olive Garden knockoff.

Her sister called me separately a couple weeks later. Asked what changed. Their mom noticed too. Apparently two women at her office who are on Ozempic asked what she was taking, and she brought the jar in to show them.

She told Diane about them last week. I overheard her on the phone saying "I know it sounds weird but just try them."

I don't know if this is the kind of thing people usually post. I'm really not a social media person. My daughter helped me figure out how to write this because she said people might need to hear it.

If you're watching someone you love shrink. And I don't mean the weight. I mean the actual person they are just getting... smaller. Quieter. Less there. And you feel like you can't do anything.

I got my wife back. Not the smaller version of her. The real one. The one who plans things and laughs too loud and spends fifteen minutes picking out a shirt for a Saturday night.

That's all I wanted. That's what this gave us.
creative.title: My wife tried Miralax, fiber powder, probiotics, and more water than I've ever seen a person drink. None of it worked — because all of it was aimed at the wrong organ.
